title: How elements take up space
sub: Measure and Arrange, alignment, Margin and Padding
cards/0/body:
Before drawing, Avalonia asks every element: "How much space do you need?" That is Measure. Then the parent decides and says: "Here is your rectangle." That is Arrange.

A button needs room for its text. How much it actually gets is up to the panel it sits in.
cards/1/q: Put the layout steps in order
cards/1/items/0: The parent asks its children how much they need (Measure)
cards/1/items/1: The children answer with their desired size
cards/1/items/2: The parent gives each one a rectangle (Arrange)
cards/1/explain: Requests go up, space is handed down.
cards/2/body: If the rectangle is bigger than the element needs, alignment decides: HorizontalAlignment = Left, Center, Right or Stretch (fill the space). Most elements default to Stretch.
cards/3/task: Right now the children sit in a row. Make each one stretch across the full window width, one below another.
cards/4/body:
Margin is space outside: from the element to its neighbors.
Padding is space inside: from the border to the content.

Syntax: "10" means all sides, "10,5" means horizontal and vertical, "10,5,10,0" means left, top, right, bottom.
cards/5/q: The buttons are stuck together. What do you add to each one to get a gap?
cards/5/explain: Padding would push the text inside the button apart, not the buttons themselves.
cards/6/options/0: 10 left and right, 5 top and bottom
cards/6/explain: Two numbers mean horizontal and vertical.
cards/7/q: A centered button with 12 of space around it
cards/7/explain: Margin is outside, Padding is inside.
cards/8/q: Match each term to its meaning
